## 5. Anomalies detected

- **draft_13**: Game D13_S4_G_Ramp vs D13_S8_GW_Counters (Turn 19): Forge's log emits two contradictory 'has won' lines — likely AI turn-timeout (120,000ms). Winner resolved via 'Match Winner -': D13_S4_G_Ramp.
- **draft_47**: Game D47_S5_GR_Stompy vs D47_S1_BG_Graveyard (Turn 15): Forge's log emits two contradictory 'has won' lines — likely AI turn-timeout (120,000ms). Winner resolved via 'Match Winner -': D47_S5_GR_Stompy.

## 6. Limitations

- **Per-card reliability**: 9 card(s) in this corpus have never been seen in more than one draft — their winrate mirrors the one deck that contained them rather than being an independent signal (see `cards.csv`, `reliable` column).

- **Color classification** excludes archetypes whose label doesn't resolve to a recognizable color prefix (e.g. a generic `Combo` label) — counted separately rather than forced into a bucket.

- **No sideboard access**: all matches are best-of-one (see `simulate.py`, `MATCHES_PER_PAIRING`). A card that only earns its keep in a specific matchup is played in every game regardless of opponent if maindecked, which can drag its measured winrate down relative to how it would perform if it could be deployed only when relevant. Testing on a small best-of-three sample found no evidence Forge's AI swaps cards between games of a match, so a longer match format is unlikely to change this on its own — see the project README for the full investigation.
